arguments.heading: Argument session of March 30, 2026
paragraphs: This was the only argument session in the record. It happened March 30, 2026, in Washington, D.C. It was not a reargument.
Jules asked the Court to reverse the judgment below. His side argued the federal court lacks power to confirm the award but may dismiss the case.

Jules argued Section 1331 does not supply jurisdiction to confirm the award. He said supplemental jurisdiction fails because there is no common nucleus of operative facts. He invoked Kokonnen's reasoning about ancillary jurisdiction.

Jules minimized the the opposing sides' practical concerns. He said federal courts can delay dismissal while parties pursue state-court confirmation. He said parallel state and federal litigation is routine.
The the opposing sides asked the federal court to enter judgment on the award and dismiss the case. They said this avoids bifurcated state and federal proceedings.
The justices tested several assumptions. One asked the purpose of a stay under FAA Section 3. One asked why confirmation is not like entering a consent decree.
One justice asked whether most arbitrations require a court to convert the award into an enforceable judgment. Another asked whether dismissal is appropriate before confirmation validates the award.
The record does not support additional arguments, facts, or responses beyond those described here. The Chief Justice stated the case was submitted at argument's close.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Adrian Jules sued Andre Balazs Properties and others. Jules is the the side that brought the case. Balazs Properties and others are the the opposing sides. The case carries docket number 25-83.
Lawyers Adam G. Unikowsky and Daniel L. Geyser argued the case in Washington, D.C. Unikowsky spoke for Jules. Geyser spoke for the the opposing sides.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 1, lines 1-9

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: Jules brought a federal employment claim. That claim was sent to arbitration. The arbitrator issued a sanctions money award against Jules.

Jules says confirming that award would turn the arbitral result into a federal judgment. A federal judgment would let the other side collect money. The lower court entered the judgment being challenged here.
The Supreme Court heard oral argument starting at 11:23 a.m. At the end, the Chief Justice said the case was submitted. That means the justices will now decide the case privately.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Jules asks the Supreme Court to reverse the judgment below. He wants the confirmation of the award undone.
The the opposing sides ask the same federal court to enter judgment on the award and dismiss the case. They say this avoids split state and federal proceedings.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Jules argues the federal court lacks jurisdiction to confirm the award. Jurisdiction means the court's legal power to hear a dispute. He says the court may dismiss the federal case instead.

Jules says a federal law, Section 1331, does not supply power to confirm the award. He says some extra basis is needed. He also says supplemental jurisdiction is unavailable because the confirmation dispute shares no common facts with the federal claim.
Jules leans on an earlier case called Kokonnen. He says confirming an award is like a contract dispute. He says it is factually separate from the underlying federal claim.
Jules downplays the the opposing sides' practical worries. He says federal courts can delay dismissal while parties use state courts. He says parallel state and federal litigation is routine.

The the opposing sides want one federal court to finish the job. They say entering judgment and dismissing the case avoids bifurcated proceedings. Bifurcated proceedings mean the dispute gets split across two court systems.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: One justice asked about the purpose of a stay under a federal arbitration law. The question probed why a court would pause a case.
A justice asked why confirming an award is not like entering a consent decree. A consent decree is a court order both sides agree to.
A justice asked whether most arbitrations need some court to turn the award into an enforceable judgment. That tested whether confirmation is a normal step.
A justice asked whether dismissal makes sense before confirmation validates the award. The question tested the order of events Jules proposes.

paragraphs: The Chief Justice said the case was submitted after argument. The justices will confer and vote privately. No outcome is known yet. Questions from the bench are not decisions or votes.
